identity.title: Core Monitoring System Software Modeling Error Results in Condition Prohibited by Technical Specifications

cause.proximate_text: GEH notified CPS the Side Entry Orifice (SEO) loss coefficient was underpredicted for some fuel bundle locations, which could result in an overprediction of MCPR margin in core monitoring applications. The overprediction was a result of not originally including in the assessment flow area restrictions associated with instrument support structures in the cross beams... a legacy vendor design calculation error.
cause.theme: vendor core-monitoring software modeling error (SEO loss coefficient underprediction)

nodes.theme: vendor core-monitoring software modeling error (SEO loss coefficient underprediction)

nodes.role: reactor core power distribution/MCPR monitoring software

properties.location: adjacent to two supporting beams of core plate, ~25% of fuel bundle locations

nodes.display_name: SEO loss coefficient underpredicted in core monitoring model
nodes.description: Flow area restrictions from instrument support structures in cross beams were not included in original assessment, causing underprediction of SEO loss coefficient.

nodes.display_name: Fuel bundle bypass flow inaccurately modeled / MCPR margin overpredicted
nodes.description: Core monitoring system did not accurately model bypass flow for bundles adjacent to two support beams, resulting in overprediction of MCPR margin (understated MFLCPR).

nodes.display_name: MFLCPR exceeded 1.0 for longer than 6 hours (undetected)
nodes.description: After applying SC 21-04 Rev.1 penalty retroactively, review showed MFLCPR was greater than 1.0 for periods on May 25, 2019, and June 22-Aug 3, 2019, exceeding the 6-hour allowed time without corrective action being taken at the time.

nodes.display_name: Multiple entries into condition prohibited by Technical Specifications (TS 3.2.2)
nodes.duration: intermittent periods across May 25, 2019 and June 22-Aug 3, 2019

nodes.display_name: Verified current MFLCPR value is within recommended limit
